content:
Use the python tool to read this CSV and create a PNG line chart.
Requirements:
- Plot monthly average temperature (Jan-Dec only; ignore Annual Mean)
- Include x/y axes and month labels
- Read the CSV, create the chart, and save it in a single Python execution; do not make preliminary inspection calls
- Save exactly one PNG file and close the figure with plt.close()
- Do not display the figure inline
- Include exactly one download link to the saved PNG in your final response

CSV:
Month,Average Temperature (°C),Deviation from 1991-2020 Norm (°C)
January,0.0,+1.5
February,1.3,+1.7
March,4.1,+1.5
April,8.2,+1.9
May,10.3,-0.2
June,17.6,+3.8
July,15.4,-0.3
August,16.4,+1.2
September,11.9,+0.5
October,7.2,-0.2
November,2.3,+0.1
December,1.3,+2.0
Annual Mean,8.0,+1.1

input.command:
cat > /tmp/chart.py << 'EOF'
import csv, io, os
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

CSV_TEXT = """Month,Average Temperature (°C),Deviation from 1991-2020 Norm (°C)
January,0.0,+1.5
February,1.3,+1.7
March,4.1,+1.5
April,8.2,+1.9
May,10.3,-0.2
June,17.6,+3.8
July,15.4,-0.3
August,16.4,+1.2
September,11.9,+0.5
October,7.2,-0.2
November,2.3,+0.1
December,1.3,+2.0
Annual Mean,8.0,+1.1
"""

MONTHS = ["January","February","March","April","May","June","July",
          "August","September","October","November","December"]

reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(CSV_TEXT))
rows = {r["Month"]: float(r["Average Temperature (°C)"]) for r in reader}
labels = [m[:3] for m in MONTHS]
values = [rows[m] for m in MONTHS]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
ax.plot(labels, values, marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#d62728", markersize=6)
ax.set_title("Monthly Average Temperature (Jan–Dec)")
ax.set_xlabel("Month")
ax.set_ylabel("Average Temperature (°C)")
ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=10)
for x, y in zip(labels, values):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), ha="center", fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()

out_dir = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_DIR", "/tmp")
out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "monthly_avg_temperature.png")
fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)
print(out_path)
EOF
python3 /tmp/chart.py && ls -la "${OUTPUT_DIR:-/tmp}"/monthly_avg_temperature.png

content.text:
I created the line chart of monthly average temperatures for January through December, with the Annual Mean row excluded. It has labeled x and y axes, three-letter month labels, and a value label on each point. The figure was closed after saving.

Download: [monthly_avg_temperature.png](/files/output/d48828cd2bb52b94/monthly_avg_temperature.png)

Note that I ran this as a Python script through the bash execution tool, since that was the only code-execution tool available to me.

content.text:
The file is **monthly_avg_temperature.png**.

The CSV has **13 data rows**, plus a header row. Twelve are the monthly rows (January through December), and the thirteenth is the Annual Mean row, which I excluded from the chart.
